notes: Categorie e tag sono revisionati editorialmente usando titolo e abstract ufficiale di ogni sessione; non sono track ufficiali Codemotion.
Il programma è una fotografia dell’HTML del 15 ottobre 2026 e può subire variazioni.
Quattro voci organizzative del Tech Lead Summit senza speaker non sono incluse nell’elenco dei talk.
Gli abstract ufficiali sono importati da Sessionize nella lingua originale, senza traduzione.

speakers.name: Abiodun Olowode
speakers.biography: Abiodun is the CTO and Co-Founder at Metrifox, where she leads the engineering team building impactful software. She specialises in streamlining workflows, reducing technical debt, and building reusable abstractions that unlock developer productivity through automation and strong defaults. She’s passionate about growing engineers and building cultures where excellence is the norm — and she writes and speaks regularly about leadership, engineering, and the uncomfortable parts of both.

speakers.name: Alessandro Festa
speakers.biography: Highly energetic, charismatic leader with Technical proficiency as well as a Business attitude. Product Manager, Coder, Passionate.

speakers.name: Alessandro Miliucci
speakers.biography: I am Alessandro Miliucci, a developer, author and speaker. Although I have many interests, software development is what I devote most of my time to and what I am best known for. I have also written a few books on software development. My interests range over all aspects of software: from user interfaces to databases, including network protocols. I am a co-organizer of RomaJS meetup and the leader of MongoDB User Group in Rome. During my career I have spent a lot of time working on start-ups such as Hype, the first Italian neo-bank, and Vidra, an e-commerce SaaS that I co-Founded. Nowadays I work as a Solution Architect for Fabrick S.p.a. one of the leading Italian Fintech companies.

speakers.name: Alessandro Riboni
speakers.biography: Alessandro Riboni is a Staff Engineer at Generali, specializing in AI engineering and GenAI platforms. Supports internal teams and builds horizontal tooling that standardizes and simplifies GenAI development: from a framework for prompt management, automated evaluation and CI/CD-based release of prompts, to Flowmetrics, a semantic layer that gives AI agents governed access to business metrics. Before that, five years in consulting for insurance and banking: first as a data engineer on real-time pipelines, then as an ML engineer building LLM-based claims assistants, RAG systems for policy risk assessment and document-parsing tools on AWS. Holds an MSc in Data Science from the University of Milano-Bicocca.

speakers.name: Alessio Acella
speakers.role: CTO, Founder, Software engineer at Omnes
speakers.biography: Alessio is CTO and Software Engineer at Omnes. Over the years, he has specialized in building tailored digital platforms, evolving from early work in C, C++, JAVA, PHP and Laravel to large-scale projects powered by modern stacks such as Vue.js, Nuxt, TypeScript, React and Node.js. His technical journey has been shaped by constant curiosity for scalable architectures and performance-driven design. Alessio has worked extensively with cloud infrastructures on AWS, relational as well as NoSQL databases, real-time messaging, and modern headless frameworks. Today he leads teams building B2B and B2C platforms that combine strong engineering foundations with a focus on user experience and accessibility, while exploring how AI and automation are reshaping development practices.

speakers.name: Alexio Cassani
speakers.biography: Alexio Cassani is an Italian entrepreneur and thought leader in generative AI, AI agents, and corporate digital transformation. He is co-founder of FairMind, a startup that is building AI agent solutions that boost software development team productivity. A Computer Engineering graduate from Politecnico di Milano (2003), he was CTO at Cortilia and Webscience (now part of the Adesso group), founded the retail and e-commerce startup Stentle (acquired in 2019), and worked as a researcher with the Intranet and Cloud Observatories at Politecnico di Milano. He is adjunct professor at Politecnico di Milano School of Management, teaching Generative AI and advising companies on AI adoption and transformation. A frequent speaker at Italian and international conferences on generative AI, AI agents, software factory innovation, and responsible technology adoption, he is the author of "Code Revealed", a guide to how roles, organization, and tools in software development are evolving in the AI era.

speakers.name: Alfonso Fuggetta
speakers.biography: Alfonso Fuggetta is a Full Professor of Computer Science at Politecnico di Milano, where his work spans software engineering and digital transformation in their technical and managerial dimensions. He is the former CEO and Scientific Director of Cefriel and former Chief Digital Transformation Officer of Ferrari, and has been a Visiting Professor at NTNU, CU Boulder, and UC Irvine. For over thirty years, he has worked at the crossroads of software engineering research, industry, and innovation, advising companies and public institutions on digital transformation and the impact of AI. He is ranked among the top 2% of researchers worldwide (Elsevier/Stanford) and writes about technology and society on his Substack, "A bassa voce".

speakers.name: Alfonso Graziano
speakers.biography: Alfonso Graziano is a AI Tech Lead with a strong background in software engineering, specializing in JavaScript, AI and distributed systems. Currently at Nearform, Alfonso leads engineering teams to deliver impactful projects. Passionate about knowledge sharing, he loves to solve problems and contributes to tech communities.

speakers.name: Alfredo Morresi
speakers.biography: I help people to get things done, at the intersection of technology, community, leadership and fun. Community builder and developer by passion, Developer Relation @ Google by profession , I love being a dad, free-software, running on the beach, snowboarding. I relentlessly train myself in preparing (and eating) Tiramisù. I’m definitely yellow.

speakers.name: Alice Viola Setti
speakers.role: Senior Staff Engineer @ Smartness, author of Queen MQ
speakers.biography: Alice Viola Setti is a proud neurodivergent transgender woman, software engineer, architect, and sysadmin with a master's degree in Mechatronic Engineering and a product-builder mindset. Her background spans the entire technical spectrum, from provisioning bare-metal datacenters to architecting complex distributed systems and leading engineering teams. She is highly autonomous and drives end-to-end product delivery. She works mainly with Kubernetes, Kafka, Postgres, C++, Node, and Vue, and has shipped with Python, Ruby, Objective-C++, Swift, Rust, OpenCV, Proxmox, VMware, Nginx, HAProxy, Scylla, Redis, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, OpenSearch, Solr, Neo4j, Cassandra, Pulsar, RabbitMQ, NATS, and MQTT. She has installed and managed clusters in on-premise datacenters using bare-metal servers, hypervisors, and Kubernetes; configured network switches and firewalls; developed microservice architectures; built drone control systems; and conducted research in computer vision.

speakers.name: Andrea Ferlito
speakers.biography: ICT professional with over 20 years experience in software design and development and project management. His insane passion for videogames brought him to be well known through the italian and international game developer communities. He is also leader of Roma Game Dev community, organizing dedicated meetups and the famous Global Game Jam. He is CTO and Game Developer Content manager of Codemotion

speakers.name: Andrea Raponi
speakers.biography: Andrea Raponi è Technical Manager in Engineering, dove si occupa di architetture software, tecnologie Cloud Native e Intelligenza Artificiale Generativa. Ha trascorso buona parte della sua carriera a metà strada tra infrastruttura e sviluppo software, con una particolare curiosità per tutto ciò che succede “sotto il cofano”. È appassionato di open source, developer experience e di tecnologie costruite senza legarsi troppo a strumenti o vendor specifici. Quando non disegna architetture o scrive codice, probabilmente sta leggendo Thoreau, andando in bici o trasformando qualche nuova ossessione tecnologica in un side project.

speakers.name: Andrei Chiș
speakers.biography: Andrei Chiș is a tool crafter at feenk (feenk.com), where he builds tools and techniques to improve software development both with and without AI. He is also a co-author of the Glamorous Toolkit (gtoolkit.org) platform.

speakers.name: Andrey Breslav
speakers.biography: Andrey created the Kotlin programming language and led its development at JetBrains from 0 to millions of users. He’s the founder of CodeSpeak, a spec-based AI coding solution.

speakers.name: Aniello Bossa
speakers.biography: Aniello Bossa è Senior Data Engineer in Generali Italia, dove progetta e gestisce microservizi e pipeline dati su Google Cloud per i processi di gestione sinistri e antifrode. Lavora ogni giorno con Python, FastAPI, Kubernetes e Airflow, e si occupa di portare in produzione sistemi affidabili e osservabili su larga scala. Crede nella semplicità, nell'automazione e nel codice che si spiega da solo.

speakers.name: Aurélie Vache
speakers.role: Developer Advocate at OVHcloud, Docker Captain, CNCF Ambassador & GDE
speakers.biography: Aurélie Vache is a Developer Advocate at OVHcloud in Toulouse, France. She is a Docker Captain, CNCF ambassador, Google Cloud Developer Expert & Women techmarkers Ambassador. She has been working as a Developer and Ops for over 20 years. Cloud enthusiast and advocates DevOps/Cloud/Golang best practices. Technical writer (dev.to/aurelievache), a book author & reviewer, a sketchnoter and a speaker at international conferences. Conferences and meetups organizer since 2016. Creator and maintainer of https://developers.events/ , a collaborative, open-source platform that aggregates & list developer/tech-focused conferences/events and call-for-papers (CFP) opportunities worldwide, helping speakers, organizers, sponsors and attendees. She created a new visual way for people to learn and understand Cloud technologies: "Understanding Kubernetes/Istio/Docker in a visual way" in sketchnotes, books and videos. Blog: https://dev.to/aurelievache/ YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/c/AurelieVache

speakers.name: Christian Schabetsberger
speakers.biography: Christian Schabetsberger, the world's okayest developer, is a Freelance Software Engineer & Architect from Linz, Austria with over a decade of experience. Having spend half of his life in the .NET ecosystem (amongst others), he likes to stay on the bleeding edge of technology to become the (tech-savvy) ninja he pretends to be since he is six. He is also an active community member, organising the .NET Meetup in Linz and supporting other local user groups. Furthermore he is a member of the .NET Foundation.

speakers.name: Costantino Cavallo
speakers.biography: Costantino Cavallo is the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer at altermAInd and an international speaker with a strong passion for technology and continuous learning. He focuses on Automation and Artificial Intelligence, helping organizations maximize team efficiency through innovative methodologies and practical adoption of emerging technologies. Deeply committed to exploring new approaches, Costantino blends strategic vision with hands-on experimentation.

speakers.name: Daniel Zotti
speakers.role: Tech Lead & Team Lead @ Bitrock, Podcaster @ Shiftati di Testa
speakers.biography: Daniel è un software engineer da quasi 20 anni, specializzato nel frontend dal lontano 2013. Si definisce un Creative Web Developer perché ama portare una visione non banale nei progetti in cui è coinvolto. Nella sua carriera ha visto di tutto: da un’azienda di 5 persone al reparto IT di un ospedale, fino a una multinazionale da 20 mila dipendenti, senza farsi mancare il “classico” anno da freelance. Dal 2021 lavora nell'area front-end di Bitrock, una società di consulenza di Milano. Fuori dall'ufficio calca i palchi come improvvisatore teatrale, e si spaccia per stand-up comedian con i Gin Comici. Insieme a Stefano conduce Shiftati di Testa: Il podcast più atteso del web (anche se il web ancora non lo sa!)

speakers.name: Daniele Zonca
speakers.biography: Daniele Zonca is a Distinguised Engineer working for Red Hat. He contributes to many open source projects like TrustyAI, KServe, vLLM and llm-d. He is the Chief Architect for Red Hat Openshift AI product and before this he led Big Data development team of one of the largest Italian bank.

speakers.name: Danilo Deponti
speakers.biography: Danilo Deponti is a Senior Software Engineer, currently working in Doctolib, where he helps build the internal AI-augmented developer tools. His work focuses on autonomous coding agents, AI orchestration, and developer productivity, turning experimental LLM tooling into something teams can trust in production. He's passionate about pushing the boundaries of what AI can do inside a real engineering organisation: from agent fleets and persistent memory to observability, cost control, and keeping humans meaningfully in the loop.

speakers.name: David McCarter
speakers.role: Microsoft MVP (Developer Technologies), Software Architect, Speaker, Trainer, Inventor, and Mentor.
speakers.biography: **As David gradually winds down his career and looks toward retirement, now is the time to benefit from his experience, insight, and availability.** David McCarter is an exceptionally seasoned software engineer, a celebrated author, and a captivating speaker with a remarkable track record spanning over two decades within the industry. Holding the distinguished title of Microsoft MVP (Most Valuable Professional), David also serves as a solutions architect, Code Quality Zar, consultant, proficient code reviewer, and the esteemed editor-in-chief of dotNetTips.com. He has left an indelible mark on user groups, educational institutions, and prominent conferences worldwide, such as BuildStuff, Øredev, NDC, Copenhagen Developers Festival, Code Camp, SQL Saturday, DevConnections, and VSLive, among others. His instructional legacy even includes a tenure at the University of California, San Diego.

speakers.name: Davide Caldarulo
speakers.biography: Davide Caldarulo is a Senior Software Developer at Objectway's Bari office, where he designs and develops Java backend solutions for the financial sector. Passionate about technology and problem-solving, he enjoys turning complex challenges into simple, efficient solutions, always striving to deliver high-quality software that creates real value.

speakers.name: Davide Pensato
speakers.biography: In 1999 Davide Pensato starts his career as in-house Audio DirectorSound Designer at Ubisoft Studios Milano. In a couple of years he is responsible of audio team. Both a creative and technical figure, he can create audio for a game as well as integrating it using software and hardware tools. In January 2007 creates his own company (dpstudios) offering consulting and services for game audio. He develops web and multimedia projects too, as a new activity branch.

speakers.name: Dennis Nerush
speakers.biography: Dennis Nerush is the Director of AI at Elementor, where he leads the company's AI strategy and guides teams through the integration of GenAI technologies that enhance productivity while preserving human creativity and accountability. With over 15 years of experience as a developer, manager, director, and adviser across multiple tech companies and startups, Dennis has dedicated his career to building people-first cultures rooted in continuous learning, curiosity, and growth. He believes that when individuals thrive, teams and businesses flourish, a philosophy that has guided him in founding dozens of teams and mentoring over 100 managers. Dennis is a seasoned public speaker and writer who shares his insights on AI integration, leadership, and team performance at international conferences. He's passionate about helping leaders develop the skills and confidence to excel in a world where human leadership and AI collaboration go hand in hand.

speakers.name: Diana Bernabei
speakers.role: CEO, Co-Founder & Senior Accessibility Engineer @ AriaLab
speakers.biography: Sono una Frontend Developer freelance specializzata in consulenza sull'accessibilità, design UI/UX e sviluppo web. Il mio obiettivo è garantire che ogni sito web sia accessibile a tutti, indipendentemente dalle capacità fisiche o cognitive. Da oltre 5 anni, mi dedico con passione e professionalità a questo obiettivo, lavorando con semplicità e attenzione al dettaglio. Per me, l'accessibilità web va oltre la tecnologia: rappresenta una questione di diritti, uguaglianza e libertà.

speakers.name: Dotan Horovits
speakers.biography: Horovits lives at the intersection of technology, product and open source. With over 20 years in the tech industry as a software developer, a solutions architect and a product manager, he brings a wealth of knowledge in cloud-native architectures, big data solutions, DevOps practices and more. Horovits is an international speaker, an Ambassador of the Cloud Native Computing Foundation, and host of the popular OpenObservability Talks podcast. On the OpenSearch front, Horovits is an OpenSearch Ambassador under the Linux Foundation, he serves as a lead for the Observability technical advisory group, and is on the project’s outreach committee. Horovits works as a senior open source advocate at Amazon Web Services, with special focus on the OpenSearch project, open observability, and open source practices.

speakers.name: Edoardo Dusi
speakers.biography: Edoardo is a Developer Relations Engineer. He has a strong software developer and team leader background, working on various projects and platforms. He is passionate about creating and sharing content that educates and inspires other developers, such as tech talks, videos, podcasts, conferences, and more. He enjoys connecting with the developer community and promoting the benefits of open source software.

speakers.name: Egon Ferri
speakers.biography: Putting AI into production is not just about connecting a model to a chat interface. In Gamindo AI, we built a workflow that turns vague requirements, source materials and live game state into structured game-based learning content: it refines the initial intent, generates a validated learning experience, supports controlled edits through structured patches, and produces contextual commentary and audio aligned with gameplay. This talk walks through the architecture behind it: typed contracts with PydanticAI, FastAPI endpoints, fallback strategies across OpenAI, Anthropic and Google, streaming events, output validation, eval datasets, custom evaluators, observability with Logfire, and practical error handling. Attendees will leave with patterns and tradeoffs for designing AI workflows that are robust, observable, measurable and flexible enough to evolve without rewriting everything.

speakers.name: Elena Guidi
speakers.biography: Senior Software Developer at Thoughtworks A developer with 8 years of experience across Italy and abroad, Elena bridges the gap between clean code and clear communication. At Thoughtworks, she balances technical delivery with a mission to debug the "Human Stack." Through the lens of Crucial Conversations and Green Computing, she equips teams to handle high-stakes friction and build a more sustainable digital future. Code is logical; people are complex. She helps you master both.

speakers.name: Emanuele Fabbiani
speakers.role: Co-founder and head of AI at xtream (acquired by TeamSystem), Professor at Catholic University of Milan
speakers.biography: Emanuele is an entrepreneur, engineer, and researcher passionate about achieving impact with AI. After earning his PhD in machine learning and working as a guest researcher at EPFL in Lausanne, he is now co-founder and Head of AI at xtream, a company that applies AI to solve complex business challenges. xtream was acquired by TeamSystem in September 2025. Emanuele is also a professor of AI at the Catholic University of Milan and has been a guest lecturer at Italian, Swiss, and Polish universities. He has published 8 papers in international journals with 175+ citations and contributed to over 30 international conferences, including AMLD Lausanne, ODSC London, WeAreDevelopers Berlin, PyData Berlin, PyData Paris, PyCon Italy, the Swiss Python Summit, and Codemotion Milan and Rome.

speakers.name: Emmanuele Villa
speakers.biography: Emmanuele Villa is a Senior Technical Consultant at Fincons Group, leading mobile and web development with technologies like Kotlin Multiplatform, Compose, and SwiftUI. He also teaches at the Università della Terza Età in Carate Brianza and is pursuing a degree in Middle Age History, bridging his passion for technology and the humanities. Outside of work, he enjoys exploring Quantum Computing, running Dungeons&Dragons, and reading One Piece.

speakers.name: Enzo Lombardi
speakers.role: Cleafy, 🌩️ Cloud Software Architect 🦀 Learning Rust 🕹️ Mame contributor 🔬 Arduino thinkerer: ESP32, nrf52 🔍 Former Google and Microsoft dev 🥞 Almost-full stack developer (can't align with CSS)

In Microsoft I was part of the original .Net team and later worked on Windows Compatibility Toolkit and Windows Performance Analyzer. In Google I worked for Hangouts during its glory days, and moved to work on the Directory product part of Google Workplace offer. I moved back to Italy in Summer 2023 to pivot my career as Software Architect in order to bring my experience to use in a fast growing company working on a interesting product. I am learning by teaching Rust and successfully contributed to Mame bringing the sound effects to the Italian arcade game dribbling. Book author of: Tu lo conosci Claude vol. 1 and 2 OOP to Rust (English and Italian) Multiplatform UI in Rust

speakers.name: Erik Pronk
speakers.biography: Erik Pronk is a passionate software engineer that has been working in IT since 2001. During this period he has gained a lot of experience in a variety of technologies, roles, development environments and market segments. His main focus is on implementing enterprise solutions in an agile way. In his spare time, Erik loves to run and experiment with VR and domotics. Erik works at JDriven where he shares his passion and drive with other colleagues.

speakers.name: Ettore Di Giacinto
speakers.biography: I’m Ettore and I’m a long-time Open Source hacker and hacktivist. I’ve been involved in the Open Source community for more than 18 years. I’ve studied CS at University, and pursued my degree at full votes with a MS in Computer Science. I formerly was a Gentoo developer, I did lead Sabayon Linux and contributed to several FOSS projects among openSUSE, Cloud Foundry, openQA, llama.cpp. Previously I’ve worked at SUSE where I was leading the Elemental team. At Spectro Cloud I've created Kairos and donated it to CNCF, and collaborated with Intel on SENA ( Secure Edge-Native Architecture). I am a Golang and Kubernetes enthusiast with a strong Linux background skillset. I am the LocalAI creator and maintainer.

speakers.name: Francesco Facconi
speakers.role: Speaker on Digitalia - Senior Engineering Manager at Doctolib
speakers.biography: Engineer, manager, former startupper, broadcasting every Monday evening on Digitalia, one of the longest-lasting Podcast in Italy, speaking about technology and how this interacts with our lives. His last book is "Almanacco Digitaliano 2024" from Ledizioni Publishing. Musician and performer with more than 400 gigs.

speakers.name: Francesco Pirrone
speakers.biography: Graduated in Computer Science from the University of Turin, he is a full-stack developer at Finwave, where he is responsible for the design and development of distributed systems. Nerd at 99%, he is trying to stay in touch with the real world for the remaining 1% of his day. Since 2018, he is one of the Community Leader for GDG Cloud Turin.

speakers.name: Gabriele Negro
speakers.biography: Gabriele is a technology leader with extensive experience in building digital platforms and enterprise software solutions. He currently works on AI-driven products focused on transforming how people learn, work, and make decisions inside organizations. With a background in software architecture and large-scale systems, he has led projects in banking, fintech, and cloud-native environments, helping companies adopt modern architectures and artificial intelligence in real business scenarios. Today his main focus is on the impact of AI on society and the workplace, exploring how tools like generative AI and vibe coding are changing the way software is built and how companies operate.

speakers.name: Gabriele Santomaggio
speakers.biography: RabbitMQ team member, working with distributed systems, open source lover, Linux fan.

speakers.name: Gianni Forlastro
speakers.role: Google GDE Cloud, Cloud Architect, GDG Cloud Torino & Flutter Torino Community Lead
speakers.biography: Inizia la sua avventura con un Intel 80386 e si laurea in Informatica all'Università di Torino che completa con due master: Comunicazione Digitale/Web Marketing e Social Media Management, il secondo in Cloud Computing. Dopo esperienze come sviluppatore web e mobile, oggi è Cloud Architect, docente e assistente universitario, co-organizzatore di droidcon Italy, Swift Heroes e Flutter Heroes. Lato community nel 2018 fonda il GDG Cloud Torino, diventa Google Champion Innovator nel 2023 e Google GDE Cloud nel 2025. Su Instagram è noto come @mosquitoman81, tra i creator italiani più seguiti su giochi e fiere.

speakers.name: Giorgio Natili
speakers.role: Head of AI Engineering for Oracle Support
speakers.biography: Giorgio Natili is a technologist, ethicist, and builder working at the intersection of artificial intelligence, human dignity, and data sovereignty. As Senior Director and Head of AI Engineering for Oracle Cloud Support, he leads the design and deployment of AI systems that make enterprise support smarter, faster, and more trustworthy at scale. His expertise in Sovereign AI—the principle that individuals, organizations, and nations must retain control over their data, models, and AI-driven decisions—comes from years of hands-on work. At OPAQUE Systems, where he served as VP and Head of Engineering, he built confidential AI infrastructure that enabled insights from sensitive data without exposing it. This shaped his belief that ethical AI and sovereign AI are inseparable. With experience at Amazon, Mozilla, Capital One, OPAQUE Systems, and Oracle, he focuses on building AI that is powerful without being exploitative.

speakers.name: Giovanni Galloro
speakers.biography: Giovanni Galloro is a Customer Engineer at Google, where he has been working since 2017. Over the years, he has built deep expertise in developer productivity and software delivery tools and practices. Today, he partners with engineering organizations across Europe to help them unlock the full potential of AI, improving how teams build, ship, and iterate on software at scale.

speakers.name: Giulio D'Alessandro
speakers.role: AI Knowledge Architect at Poste Italiane
speakers.biography: Giulio D'Alessandro is a philosophy graduate who turned to software. He joined Poste Italiane five years ago and started out as a DevOps engineer. Then AI arrived and sent him back where he began. When machines can build anything, the rare skill is knowing what's worth building — and why. He now works in Poste Italiane's Digital Technology Office, between the rigour of formal models and the messiness of what people actually mean.

speakers.name: Giulio Sciarappa
speakers.role: Enterprise Architect, Head of Azure & AI
speakers.biography: Enterprise architect with multiple job experiences in different fields, from banking to aerospace, with a spice of DevOps and other less known methodologies

speakers.name: Graziano Casto
speakers.role: Developer Relations Engineer @ Akamas | Tech Lead @ CNCF TAG DevEx | Kubernetes v1.35 Comms Lead
speakers.biography: Graziano is a DevRel Engineer at Akamas, where he spends his days convincing computers to stop being lazy and start being efficient. A former distributed systems developer and product manager, he’s now on a mission to optimize the entire cloud-native universe, one Pod at a time. As a Tech Lead for the CNCF TAG DevEx and a member of the Kubernetes Release Team since v1.34, he balances deep infrastructure roots with a passion for developer happiness. Obsessed with AI, Platform Engineering, and saving the planet through better code, Graziano is basically trying to make the cloud faster, greener, and significantly less annoying for everyone. More on: https://castograziano.com/

speakers.name: Gregorio Palamà
speakers.role: GDE Cloud | Senior Enterprise Architect @ adesso.it | Community Manager @ GDG Pescara
speakers.biography: I have been working in the IT industry for over 15 years. I currently hold the role of Senior Enterprise Architect in adesso.it. I am a Google Developer Expert on GCP and a Google Cloud Innovator Champion on the topic of modern architecture. I manage GDG Pescara together with other developers, I love sharing my knowledge and trying to do it in a fun way.

speakers.name: Guglielmo Fancellu
speakers.role: AI Knowledge Architect at Poste Italiane
speakers.biography: Guglielmo studied philosophy, then became a software architect at Poste Italiane. Over time the focus shifted toward AI and language models, with a growing interest in computational linguistics. These days the work is ontology design: building semantic models that help machines understand what people actually mean. Turns out Plato comes in handy after all

speakers.name: Jigyasa Grover

She is author of the well received O'Reilly book Practical Data Privacy (O'Reilly 2023) and has more than 10 years experience in machine learning/AI where she has helped build large scale AI systems with privacy and security built in. You can follow her work via her newsletter, Probably Private or on her website at https://kjamistan.com .

speakers.name: Laura Miranda
speakers.role: C-Level Consultant, Marketing Manager, Digital Enthusiast
speakers.biography: Ha sempre vissuto la passione per il marketing e la Comunicazione come uno strumento di Business Development. Avere un sogno, trasformarlo in obiettivi sfidanti, analizzare e pianificare le attività cercando sempre elementi di disruption e costruire un team unito. Il suo approccio al management l' ha portato a svolgere tante belle esperienze all'estero dove ha aperto la mente a stili di vita e modi di pensare differenti. Dopo una parentesi imprenditoriale, ha deciso di tornare in Italia mettendo la sua esperienza a supporto della Digital Trasformation delle PMI. Le piacciono le persone, ama ascoltare e leggere tanto. Se hai un sogno... make it happen!

speakers.name: Leonardo Cavagnis
speakers.biography: Since 2023, I have been working as a firmware engineer at Arduino, contributing to the development of innovative hardware and software solutions. I hold a Master's Degree in Computer Engineering from Politecnico di Milano, specializing in embedded systems. Before joining Arduino, I gained experience in various fields, including industrial, automotive, and green mobility. Passionate about technical writing and traveling, I am always seeking new experiences and knowledge.

speakers.name: Luca Bianchi

sessions.title: I spy on my agents and you can too!

summary.text: In this keynote, you'll take a look at why agents are worth spying on, bringing observability engineering into AI and agentic systems. Make sure your data and your tokens are doing what you think they are, and investigate how creating more visibility into agents helps you decide how to shape your agentic workflows and shift them to new settings.

sessions.title: AI is changing your team more than your code

summary.text:
AI is changing how we build software, but the biggest shift isn't in our codebases. It's between people. Every time a developer asks an AI instead of a colleague, something small breaks: a conversation that never happens, a mentoring moment that gets skipped, shared context that never forms.

This talk digs into what we're losing. The isolation paradox, where you're more productive but more alone. The echo chamber, where AI agrees instead of pushing back. The knowledge transfer gap, where juniors ship code without understanding why it works. And a quiet hit to psychological safety, especially for mid-level developers stuck between "I should know this" and "I need help."

This isn't an anti-AI talk. AI removes real barriers for non-native speakers, introverts, and teams stuck in "my idea vs. yours" debates. The difference is whether your team treats AI as a shared resource or a private shortcut.

sessions.title: Designing Physical AI Systems: From Sensors to On-Device Intelligence

summary.text:
Building AI systems on edge devices requires a different engineering mindset.
In this talk, we explore how to design Physical AI systems end-to-end, focusing on the constraints and trade-offs of moving from cloud to embedded environments.
Starting from a real architecture on Arduino platforms, we’ll walk through the full pipeline: data acquisition, preprocessing, model deployment, and on-device optimization.
The session highlights practical design decisions, latency vs accuracy trade-offs, and the challenges of running reliable AI directly on hardware.

sessions.title: Kill the Standup: How One Engineer Ships What Five Cannot

summary.text:
Fred Brooks named the problem in 1975. Communication channels grow as n(n-1)/2, and every methodology since has been a coping mechanism. None solved it.
AI has changed the equation. The cave engineer, one skilled developer with autonomy, taste, and an AI that removes the throughput constraint, now ships in two weeks what a team ships in two months. Over three months from Christmas 2025, I added nineteen thousand lines to the Node.js Virtual File System. Alone. The architecture is coherent because no team was there to mirror.
The model rests on autonomy and taste. Remove either and it breaks. I introduced CVE-2026-2581 into Undici with an AI-assisted PR I did not review properly. That is autonomy without taste. Cave engineering is the opposite.
I will cover Conway’s Law, why Scrum taxes the absence of trust, and when the cave is the wrong call. The team of one was always magical. We finally have the tools to scale it.

sessions.title: Startup veloci, Pod snelli: In-Place Pod Resize in pratica

summary.text:
I runtime moderni soffrono di un "resource gap" critico: all'avvio richiedono un picco di CPU enorme per la compilazione JIT o il caricamento delle dipendenze, per poi assestarsi pochi secondi dopo su uno steady state molto più contenuto. Finora l'unica soluzione era dimensionare i Pod sul picco, sprecando migliaia di core nei cluster.

Con l'In-Place Pod Resize di Kubernetes v1.35 possiamo finalmente implementare una strategia di startup boost. Questa sessione va oltre la teoria e si concentra sul "come" tecnico. Vedremo come costruire un workflow reattivo che assegna molte risorse all'avvio e poi riduce il footprint in modo trasparente tramite la subresource resize.

Vedremo anche come scegliere il momento giusto per recuperare le risorse, così da evitare un throttling aggressivo della CPU subito dopo il boot. Infine confronteremo diversi pattern di implementazione: patch gestite da un sidecar, un boost-operator dedicato e il Vertical Pod Autoscaler nativo. L'obiettivo è che le applicazioni non solo partano velocemente, ma restino anche stabili.

sessions.title: System Failure: Why Your Tech Stack Can't Fix a Communication Leak

summary.text:
Not everything that breaks a team can be fixed with better tools, cleaner code, or more robust testing. Sometimes, the most critical "bug" lies in the conversations we avoid, the feedback we mismanage, or the issues we raise too late. When disagreements arise, emotions run high, and the stakes are significant, we often default to two extremes: staying silent or saying it poorly.

In this session, you’ll learn how to identify these "critical path" conversations and handle them with clarity and less emotional fatigue.

We will move beyond vague advice and dive into a practical framework to:

- Debug the interaction
- Restore Safety
- Speak Truth without Damage
- From Friction to Action
- Real experiences

When the bottleneck isn't the tech stack, the ability to navigate the human stack is the most valuable skill you can develop. This talk is for anyone who wants to stop recurring conflicts and start building a culture of radical, respectful clarity.

sessions.title: We Review Code. Why Won’t We Review Each Other?

summary.text:
We review code all day, commenting on abstractions, naming, tests, and patterns. But in standups, when someone derails the meeting, we stay quiet. In design reviews, when key requirements are ignored, we assume someone else will speak up. Often, no one does, and the design ships anyway.

Engineers are confident giving feedback in pull requests, yet oddly silent everywhere else: standups, design reviews, pairing sessions, Slack threads, retros, and one-on-ones. The same people who request changes in code reviews often soften, defer, or redirect hard conversations to managers who lack context.

This session is about closing that gap. It argues for being willing to say the hard thing in the moment, clearly and constructively, outside the PR. We will explore why developers avoid these conversations, what effective directness looks like beyond code review, and how to build that skill without becoming that person everyone dreads working with.

sessions.title: Your GPU node is a snowflake: shipping AI infrastructure as a versioned artifact

summary.text:
Run a fleet of GPU or edge inference nodes and you learn the stack is brittle: one mismatch across kernel, NVIDIA driver, CUDA, firmware, runtime or, at the edge, JetPack turns a working node into a debugging session. Rebuilding that state through runtime configuration lets drift creep back, until every node is its own special case.

This talk argues for a different model: the machine becomes a versioned, reproducible image that can be shipped and rolled back atomically. When a vendor supports a specific Ubuntu-based stack, preserve it while adding an immutable lifecycle. Using Kairos as a concrete example, we will examine how to compose a reproducible AI node image, what belongs in it, and how this model changes upgrades, rollback and fleet visibility across datacenter and edge deployments.

If your AI stack needs machine-level compatibility, can your OS lifecycle reproduce it?

sessions.title: Agents Don't Work Alone

summary.text: The industry talks about agents as autonomous digital workers, but no useful worker operates in isolation. Agents depend on colleagues, tools, information, processes and supervision. This talk translates that organizational reality into software architecture, showing how an AI OS combines multi-agent collaboration, workflow engines, enterprise systems, data, user interfaces and human control.

sessions.title: Bring Your Own Agent: Building Real-World Agents for a Sovereign SDLC

summary.text:
To stay agile and maintain digital sovereignty, developers must fully own their Agentic Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), treating AI agents like any other software artifact, with modular architectures, standardized workflows, and robust automated testing.
This talk explores how to architect a "Bring Your Own Agent" (BYOA) ecosystem using open frameworks and standards. We will demonstrate the Agentic SDLC in action by walking through a real-world engineering workflow: transforming Requests for Enhancements (RFEs) into fully realized features and releases using autonomous agents.
Crucially, we will dive into Agent Evals—the CI/CD of the AI world—showing how to programmatically evaluate and score agent outputs to ensure safety, accuracy, and code quality before merging.
You will leave the session with actionable architectural patterns to standardize your agentic SDLC, implement rigorous evals, and deploy agents that genuinely accelerate your development cycles.

sessions.title: Distributed Locks with MongoDB

summary.text:
Managing shared resources in Distributed Systems is hard.
Distributed Locks are a great solution, but there's a problem: they're difficult too.
A common solution is to use a specialized software to get them but now you have another software to deploy in production just to use locks!

In this talk we will discover how to create Distributed Locks using only core MongoDB features and a few clever lines of code.
At the same time we will prove how the Safety and Liveness properties you want from a Distributed Lock are all valid (Mutual exclusion, Deadlock free and Fault tolerance).
In this way you can rely on your usual database to have Distributed Locks available for free!

sessions.title: Everything is slop, let's slow the f**k down

summary.text:
Your OSS project is flooded with agent-generated slop issues and PRs? Your wonderful experience with coding agents in a hobby greenfield project did not translate to your production codebase, and instead turned it into a beautiful shit flower of complexity?

Then this talk is the right support group for you. Come with me on a journey through how OSS and the software development lifecycle have changed for the worse, why coding agents compound our worst habits at machine speed, and how we might claw back some discipline, agency, and sanity while still benefiting from our new agentic friends.

sessions.title: Fast & Furious LLM: Scaling Performance with MTP Drafters

summary.text:
The traditional autoregressive nature of Large Language Models, generating one token at a time, creates a massive bottleneck for production workloads, heavily constrained by memory bandwidth. As models grow, scaling inference while maintaining low latency becomes one of the most complex engineering challenges.

Gemma 4 solves this bottleneck head-on by integrating native MTP drafters, revolutionizing the concept of speculative decoding. Instead of relying on a separate, smaller draft model with the associated alignment overhead, it is architected to predict multiple future tokens simultaneously, drastically accelerating generation speed without sacrificing output quality.

In this session, we will explore the mechanics of MTP drafters and we will dissect how this architecture optimizes compute resources, maximizes memory bandwidth utilization, and redefines performance benchmarks for open-weights models.

sessions.title: Racing the beam

summary.text:
Nel 1977 Atari rilasciò una console leggendaria: il VCS 2600. La RAM era misurata in byte, 128 in tutto, senza la possibilità di avere un frame buffer e con capacità grafiche molto limitate: 2 sprite giocatore, due sprite proiettile, uno sprite "palla", playground a media risoluzione.
Durante gli anni '80 coi miei amici si spendeva interi pomeriggi a giocare un gioco "oscuro" chiamato "Slot Racers" scritto dallo stesso autore del mitico Adventure, Warren Robinett. L'unico limite: richiedeva 2 giocatori, non c'era spazio per l'AI.
Nel talk mostrerò come ho:
* creato un MCP che interfacciasse Claude con l'emulatore di Atari 2600 scritto in Go per debuggare l'assembly del gioco (in precedenza da me reverse engineered a manella)
* chiedere a Claude di usare l'MCP per creare una AI che fosse abbastanza tosta da dare filo da torcere

sessions.title: Stop Grepping, Start Reasoning: Skill-Based Agentic SRE 🚀

summary.text: Let’s be honest: debugging production at scale is manual labor. 🫠 At Google, we decided making thousands of SREs act like human search engines in 2026 was a bug, not a feature. Enter the Agentic SRE Extension—a skill-based framework that lives in your terminal and actually knows its way around Kubernetes. 🚀 In this high-energy deep dive, I’m showing you exactly how we use modular skills and MCP to chain diagnostic tools, analyze metric regressions, and execute safe mitigations (Rollbacks, Throttling) without the "deleted production" anxiety. 🔥 We’ll dissect the "Outage Investigator" agent's logic loop, see it draft a technical postmortem in seconds, and discuss why we built this as a portable framework whose skills can be easily leveraged by any modern AI harness. You’ll leave with the code to wire up your own Kubernetes stack and let the agent's skills do the heavy lifting while you drink espresso. ☕️ No fluff, no 101s. Just AI agents, specialized skills, and less toil.

sessions.title: 5 API per mettere a sicuro il tuo progetto digitale

summary.text:
Il tuo utente è davvero chi dice di essere? Il numero di telefono è reale? L'email è affidabile? L'IP nasconde un comportamento sospetto? L'azienda esiste davvero? E quel documento è autentico?

La sicurezza di un progetto digitale non si ferma a login e password. In questo talk vediamo come costruire un security layer API-first per verificare utenti, aziende e operazioni lungo il funnel, dalla registrazione alla firma del contratto o all'acquisto.

Partiremo dalla verifica d'identità, tra analisi del documento, check antifrode e liveness. Vedremo poi come verificare email, telefono, IP e URL per individuare segnali di rischio in anticipo.

Affronteremo KYC e KYB con dati ufficiali e screening su sanction list, PEP e adverse media, fino a SMS OTP e firma elettronica.

Focus pratico: API REST, esempi di integrazione, flussi reali e trade-off tra sicurezza, compliance e UX.

L'obiettivo? Aggiungere un security layer completo al progetto, un'API alla volta, senza sviluppare tutto da zero.

sessions.title: Coding, but Make It Art

summary.text:
Art speaks to the fundamental creative urge in people. It comes in many forms, and it's everywhere. It's in the way we write code, design systems and build tools.

When I started my journey as an artist, I couldn’t leave my love for technology behind. This talk is about how that love of programming, combined with machinery and 3D modeling, has helped me develop a distinct style of art that's a natural blend of both painting and engineering.

In this session, I’ll talk about my inspirations and how my fascination with mathematics and art led me to build a tool for generating sketches. I’ll show how I process data with OpenAI’s models, use Azure Cosmos DB to store it, run semantic searches on embeddings, and turn that processed data into mathematical visualizations using the p5.js library.

You’ll hear the story of how I became an artist, seeing in detail how I bring shapes to life on canvas, the machines I use to do it, and how I built the system behind my generative art and paintings.

sessions.title: Developer Experience 2.0: progettare software nell’era degli AI Agents

summary.text:
L’AI sta ridefinendo il modo in cui il software viene progettato, compreso e mantenuto. Non è più soltanto di autocomplete o chatbot integrati negli IDE: l’industria sta entrando nell’era dell’AI-Augmented Development, dove agenti intelligenti collaborano attivamente con gli sviluppatori per analizzare codebase, generare documentazione, spiegare architetture e accelerare attività di debugging e refactoring.

Il talk esplorerà come strumenti come CodeWiki, MCP, Skills ed altre piattaforme AI moderne stiano trasformando la Developer Experience attraverso workflow sempre più intelligenti e conversazionali.

Una demo pratica mostrerà come utilizzare l’AI per comprendere grandi repository, creare knowledge base automatiche, interrogare il codice in linguaggio naturale e migliorare onboarding e produttività dei team.

La sessione è pensata per sviluppatori, tech lead e innovatori interessati a comprendere come gli AI Agents stiano cambiando il futuro dell’ingegneria del software.

sessions.title: From Code Velocity to Production Value

summary.text: AI is reshaping the entire software development lifecycle, from requirements and design to coding, testing, review, deployment and operations. As AI agents become active participants in software engineering, traditional processes, controls and metrics are no longer sufficient on their own. This talk explores what an AI-native SDLC looks like, how engineering practices must evolve around automation, verification, governance and observability, and how new metrics can help measure real production outcomes rather than simple code generation.

sessions.title: Green Prompting: designing AI interactions with sustainability in mind

summary.text:
Everyone uses AI, from highly skilled tech enthusiasts to individuals with few digital skills.

We’ve all heard about the importance of prompt engineering, and that writing "good" prompts leads to higher-quality responses from LLMs. We’ve also heard about AI's significant environmental impact.

But what if we could combine these two aspects and create prompts that align with sustainable goals?

In this session, I will introduce green prompting and share instructions that anyone can apply. I will show that, by carefully crafting prompts, it is possible to reduce the environmental footprint of AI systems while maintaining high-quality results.

sessions.title: Understanding at machine speed with thousands of contextual tools

summary.text:
As AI accelerates code generation, it becomes impossible to ignore the real bottleneck in software development: making sense of systems. Code reading never really worked as a scalable solution and we should stop relying on it as the primary means of informing ourselves about systems. Instead, we should augment human cognition with deterministic, contextual tools built for each problem that compress the system around the question at hand and help both humans and AI reason faster.

We call this Moldable Development. It enables teams to see their systems clearly and answer questions quickly. These contextual tools do not help only people: they also help AI agents make sense of systems. Spread throughout the system, they become skills and form an extensible kind of agent memory.

What exactly is a contextual tool? Come to the talk to see live examples built with Glamorous Toolkit, the open-source environment that helps you understand and steer systems through thousands of contextual tools.

sessions.title: Documents Are Not Knowledge: Modelling Extraction as an Event-Driven Domain

summary.text:
Chunk, embed, retrieve, hope. Standard knowledge extraction works in every demo contest, but not when you have to do it properly to map domain expertise.

We rebuilt extraction as an event-driven domain: knowledge artifacts as first-class entities with identity, span-level provenance, and a lifecycle (proposed, verified, contested, superseded). Our approach walks every document composing the domain through six layer: source, structure, claims, entities, policies, executable workflow.

The core idea: treat knowledge base as a replayable projection over an immutable log, not a database to be migrated. Then we built an harness, specific to domain knowledge, to handle per-layer golden sets, drift detection, and facts.

In this session, you will be guided into Knowledge Management in the era of AI, where agents can speed the process, and when they introduce noise in the process. The result is an artifact suitable to be consumed to build expertise aware agents.

sessions.title: Emergency in production: how to survive disasters ...a small guide

summary.text:
It's 3 AM. Your phone is ringing. The on-call alert is screaming. Production is down.
What do you do next?
Emergency responders, paramedics, firefighters, rescue teams, have faced this question for decades. They didn't solve it with better tools. They solved it with protocols, mindset, and training.
In this session we'll draw an unexpected parallel between managing a production incident and what it means to be a first responder. From triage to chain of command, from stabilizing before diagnosing to the blameless debrief: the patterns are surprisingly the same, and surprisingly absent in most engineering teams.
We'll explore:
Why triage matters more than speed when everything is on fire
How checklists and runbooks are the engineering equivalent of emergency protocols
The golden rule: stabilize first, understand later
Why communication beats heroism in a war room
How to learn from disasters without pointing fingers

sessions.title: Engineering Leadership Through Multi-Agent Simulations

summary.text:
The transition from a senior technical contributor to an effective leader is often the most jarring pivot in an engineer's career. While we have CI/CD pipelines to test our code, how do we reliably "test" our empathy, conflict resolution, and strategic team-building skills before deploying them in production with real humans?
In this session, we will explore the architecture and psychology behind a custom-built AI application designed to simulate high-stakes leadership challenges. Rather than relying on static multiple-choice tests, this platform utilizes advanced AI agent orchestration to create dynamic, interactive scenarios. Attendees will see firsthand how the application places users in complex team-building dilemmas, forcing them to make difficult management decisions in real-time.
You will learn how the system evaluates human input, cross-references decisions against established business and leadership frameworks, and generates personalized, critical insights for improvement.

sessions.title: How Does AI Watermarking Work? A Close Look at SynthID

summary.text:
Watermarking is the only reliable way to spot AI-generated content.

This talk analyses SynthID, the watermarking scheme DeepMind built for Gemini.

The core idea is tournament sampling: at each step of text generation, candidate tokens drawn from the model's output probability distribution are scored with pseudorandom values, and the token that wins the tournament gets emitted. This process leaves the model's output distribution unchanged, so watermarked text reads exactly like unwatermarked text. In DeepMind's own evaluation, the scheme added only 0.57% latency overhead per token, detected watermarked text with about 95% accuracy at a 1% false-positive rate, and caused no quality drop across 20 million Gemini responses.

The talk ends with a live demo: watermarking and detecting text on a local model with an open-source Python package.

Attendees will leave knowing exactly how the algorithm embeds and detects its signal, and how to add the same capability to a model they control.

sessions.title: Kafka didn't fit our LLM agents, so we wrote our own broker

summary.text:
One year ago we were building a runtime for LLM agents. Each session needed its own ordered queue, and one slow tool call couldn't stall everyone else. Kafka hashes your keys onto a fixed set of partitions, which makes head-of-line blocking unavoidable. So we wrote our own broker for agents. It became general-purpose, and it now powers almost every product at Smartness.
Every session, customer or order gets its own partition, created by its first message. We've run 10M of them in one queue at 1M msg/s. Each step is a transaction: the ack, the state change and the next events all commit or none do. It's one binary on its own Raft log, Kafka clients can talk to it, and it's battle-tested with Jepsen.
I'll show the code, our benchmarks against Kafka and Pulsar, and what I'd do differently.

sessions.title: The Cost of Cheap Code

summary.text: Se l’AI abbassa drasticamente il costo di produrre codice, il vantaggio competitivo non sarà avere team che sviluppano di più, ma organizzazioni capaci di trasformare quella velocità in valore senza moltiplicare complessità, rischio e debito tecnico. In questo talk vedremo come cambiano operating model, metriche, governance e competenze quando il coding smette di essere il collo di bottiglia, e quali decisioni devono prendere oggi CTO, engineering leader e manager per evitare che più output significhi semplicemente più software da mantenere.

sessions.title: Warp Pipes and Prefetching: Navigating the Web at Mario Speed

summary.text:
Long wait times are the "Bowser" of the good user experience. Even if your site looks great, slow transitions or blank loading screens can make users feel like they’ve fallen down a bottomless pit. But what if your website could predict the future and move between pages as smoothly as a Warp Pipe?

In this session, we’ll explore the "Power-Up" duo of modern web development:
- Speculation Rules API: See how prefetching and prerendering can load pages before users click.
- View Transition API: Use animations to help users move smoothly through your "world map" with ease.

We’ll break down the technical plumbing required to make these APIs work nicely together. You will leave this session with the cheat codes needed to deliver a fast, seamless experience that will have your users saying, "Mamma Mia, that’s fast!"

sessions.title: Weapon or Tool? An Ontological Approach to Enterprise Knowledge

summary.text: Today we ask LLMs and RAG pipelines to query the knowledge of large companies. That knowledge lives in unstructured silos with no shared schema, and the same term means different things to different teams. Unfortunately, LLMs are fluent about the world and clueless about your company. Ontologies were supposed to bridge that gap, yet enterprise ontologies have almost always failed. This talk is about Ousia, the semantic ontology of Poste Italiane, and how an idea, not a bigger GPU, made it work.

sessions.title: Da settimane a ore: modernizzare i report finanziari per WCAG con la GenAI

summary.text:
Nel mondo enterprise, i sistemi di reporting sono spesso i giganti silenziosi del debito tecnico. Quando si profilano nuovi requisiti di accessibilità, modernizzare centinaia di template complessi e formattati (come quelli della libreria Jasper Reports) per soddisfare gli standard di conformità WCAG può sembrare una partita impossibile. E se potessi affidare questo rompicapo a un agente basato su Intelligenza Artificiale?

In questa sessione vi guideremo attraverso il percorso con cui abbiamo modernizzato il nostro portfolio di report dei clienti, condividendo come abbiamo addestrato e ottimizzato una pipeline di migrazione guidata dall'IA generativa, capace di ricomporre un puzzle ottimizzato.

I partecipanti torneranno a casa con un esempio pratico di come usare la IA per affrontare scenari di modernizzazione dove sembra troppo difficile ricomporre i pezzi, ma la IA può aiutare a trovare l'incastro perfetto.

sessions.title: E se deployare workload AI non fosse poi così complicato?

summary.text: In questa sessione vi faremo vedere come costruire un'infrastruttura AI in pochi click, renderla scalabile e gestible e, sopratutto, ripetibile ancora e ancora. Vi faremo vedere come SUSE AI Factory with NVIDIA rende semplice e sicuro gestire i workload AI e come attraverso i suoi blueprint è semplice costruire la vostra infrastruttura AI.

sessions.title: Is getting hot in here

summary.text:
“Temperature” is one of the most quoted, misunderstood, and casually abused settings in the world of large language models. People turn it up for creativity, down for precision, and often treat it like a magic knob for “better results.” But what does temperature actually do?

This talk unpacks the real role of temperature in LLMs: how it affects token selection, why it changes the balance between predictability and variation, and when it matters less than people think.

sessions.title: The Ethics Layer: Architecting Sovereign AI and Digital Dignity in Agentic Systems

summary.text:
As we deploy autonomous AI agents globally, a critical friction point has emerged: these systems are fundamentally rooted in reinforcement learning that ruthlessly optimizes for generalized, monolithic reward functions. Consequently, they inherently clash with diverse global cultures, laws, and Sovereign AI mandates, threatening Digital Dignity.
To solve this, agentic systems require an Immutable Ethics Policy Layer (IEPL). While semantic filters (like Llama Guard) provide necessary moderation at the perception level, they fail during autonomous execution. Relying on a reasoning engine to self-police inevitably leads to hallucinated compliance.
This session introduces the IEPL—a deterministic control point between agent orchestration and tool execution. Grounded in foundational frameworks like The Human Blueprint, the IEPL shifts the AI from a general-purpose processor to a "Loyal Agent" bound by a fiduciary duty to the user.

sessions.title: Transformers Are Changing: Inside the New Architecture of Long-Context AI

summary.text:
For years, the Transformer block looked fixed: attention, feed-forward network, normalisation, and one residual stream. That design is changing.

This talk follows two shifts behind modern long-context models. First, the residual stream: each transform layer must “build knowledge” without destroying information that later layers may need. With one path, these goals compete. Multiple paths reduce this pressure by letting the model keep, change, and combine information at different depths. We will use Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections as a concrete example.

Second, attention is becoming a retrieval over working memory. As models work with code, documents, and tools, context becomes central. Standard attention cannot scale to million-token contexts, so we will present the recent Compressed Sparse Attention design implemented by DeepSeek.

The goal is to understand what is changing inside Transformers, why now, and with what trade-offs.

sessions.title: Unleash Your Inner Rockstar: The 5 Steps to Dynamic Public Speaking!

summary.text:
Ready to elevate your career, captivate your workplace, or take the leap into the world of conference speaking? This session is for you! With over 30 years of experience in public speaking, I'm thrilled to share the essential five steps that will transform you into a dynamic speaker and presenter.

If you’re like I was at the start of my journey—nervous, unsure, and wondering how to capture the audience's attention—this session will help you conquer those fears. My unique approach to public speaking has not only helped me overcome stage fright but has also allowed me to build an impactful career as an award-winning developer, university educator, published author, blogger, patented inventor, and more!

This session isn’t just about speaking; it’s about empowering yourself and enhancing your career. Come join me for this electrifying talk, and let’s unlock your potential as a rockstar speaker, elevating your communication skills to new heights and amplifying your engineering expertise!

sessions.title: Da feature a revenue: come i team tecnici possono pensare (anche) da marketer

summary.text:
Molti team di sviluppo costruiscono prodotti eccellenti, ma faticano a comunicare perché quelle funzionalità dovrebbero contare per clienti. Il risultato è un gap crescente tra valore creato e percepito.
In questo talk esploreremo un modello semplice immediato per trasformare una feature in una proposta di valore comprensibile a chi prende decisioni di acquisto. Partiremo da casi reali in ambito software B2B per mostrare come mappare in pochi passaggi feature → beneficio → problema del cliente → impatto sul business. Vedremo gli errori più comuni quando i team tecnici presentano roadmap o innovazioni (troppo linguaggio tecnico, poca centratura sul pain point) e come evitarli.
L’obiettivo è dare ai developer, ai tech lead strumenti concreti per raccontare meglio ciò che costruiscono, aumentare l’adozione delle loro soluzioni . Un cambio di prospettiva che non chiede ai tecnici di "fare marketing", ma di usare un linguaggio che amplifica il valore del loro lavoro.

sessions.title: Can an LLM understand your car? Real telemetry and predictive insights

summary.text:
Modern cars produce far more data than what appears on the dashboard: sensor readings, diagnostic codes, pressure changes, temperature values, service intervals, and component health trends.

In this talk, we’ll explore how to turn telemetry collected from different real Porsche sports cars into clear, useful insights using a structured LLM-based analysis pipeline. We’ll detect measurable signals such as declining health, warning states, critical sensors, performance patterns, and upcoming maintenance needs. Then we’ll use an LLM as an explanation layer to summarize driving behavior, anomalies, and maintenance signals.

The goal is not to let the LLM control the car or replace expert inspection, but to make complex telemetry easier to understand, explain, and act on.

sessions.title: Stop Sending Everything to the Cloud: Hybrid AI with LocalAI

summary.text:
Does every AI request really need a massive model running in the cloud?

In this talk, we'll build a hybrid, distributed AI architecture with LocalAI: small and fast models running directly at the edge, with harder tasks dynamically offloaded to larger models running on your own infrastructure.

Using a real voice assistant as our use case, we'll explore the key engineering question: where should inference run? We'll look at routing strategies, distributed inference across heterogeneous nodes, and the trade-offs between latency, model quality, resource usage, and cost.

We'll also cover what didn't work, what we learned, and real-world performance.

The result: a local-first AI architecture spanning edge devices and powerful GPU nodes, without making the cloud a requirement.

sessions.title: The Memedex: indicizzare Internet, un meme alla volta

summary.text:
I meme sembrano caos: immagini riciclate, testi sovrapposti, sottoculture, remix e inside joke. Con The Memedex abbiamo provato a trasformare questo caos in un database navigabile.

Nato da una tesi universitaria sulla storia e sulla cultura dei meme, il progetto è diventato una pipeline per raccogliere, catalogare, filtrare e moderare milioni di immagini tramite AI.

In questo talk racconteremo le sfide tecniche dietro il progetto: raccolta da fonti eterogenee, deduplicazione, classificazione per sottoculture, moderazione automatica, controllo dei costi AI e uso di embedding e grafi per trovare meme simili.

sessions.title: When AI agents click buy: atomic checkouts for dynamic retail carts

summary.text:
AI agents are moving beyond product discovery and into purchasing. That shift exposes a weak spot in today’s retail checkout systems.

In fashion retail this assumption is especially fragile: prices change, loyalty discounts expire, sizes disappear from inventory. A five-item cart can become a three-item order moments before payment authorization.

This talk looks at a specific problem in agentic commerce: how to connect a cryptographically signed, immutable payment mandate to a checkout session that is constantly changing, without freezing every transaction or approving something the user did not intend.

Using UCP for commerce orchestration and AP2 mandates for verifiable payment authority, we will examine the design of a merchant-side system for high-churn fashion catalogs.

The session includes a reference implementation that focuses on the failure modes that show up in real checkout flows. We will face what may fail when autonomous purchasing meets production retail systems.

sessions.title: When the Backlog Dispatches Itself: a Production Fleet of Autonomous AI Coding Agents

summary.text:
Are you tired of having an infinite backlog where people lose track of tickets? Do you feel you don't have enough workforce to tackle it? Sprint plannings taking forever? So did we!

We embraced the problem and dove into AI-augmented automation to get tickets tackled FAST and turn months into days. The journey wasn't easy though, and we had to learn many critical lessons along the way when dabbling with AI orchestration, verifiable identities, persistent memory, red commits handling, making sure agents don't get stuck, figuring out where to put humans in the loop for best efficiency, and much, much more.

This talk walks you through our journey, clearly identifying all the key tenets and highlighting critical aspects such as security boundaries, cost optimization, observability, along with important pitfalls and numerous protips. Blazing through that backlog won't ever be the same.

sessions.title: Future of Programming: What's our place in the world of coding machines?

summary.text:
Programming is obviously changing: more and more code is generated by agents and LLMs, people often struggle to keep up with code reviews, and overall building software feels incredibly easy to more and more people.

What is the role of humans in the future of software engineering? Can agents just do all the planning, coding, reviewing, and testing? What do humans have that LLMs don’t?

In this talk, I’ll share my take on what can and can not be, at least until Skynet has actually taken over :)

sessions.title: What Could Possibly Go Wrong? A Crash Course in Paranoia for Developers

summary.text:
Your code compiles. Your tests pass. Your deployment is green. So why are you in a meeting with Legal?

Some disasters begin with perfectly working software—and a developer who thought “someone else is handling that.”

In this talk, Matteo Flora explores ten “what could possibly go wrong?” scenarios behind everyday engineering decisions: the data you collect, the dependencies you trust, the permissions you grant, and the shortcuts that become production infrastructure. Discover the regulatory blind spots that turn ordinary technical choices into expensive surprises.

At the heart of it all: human error, misplaced confidence, and how quickly “it should be fine” becomes an incident report.

The takeaway? Paranoia as preventive practice: question defaults, challenge assumptions, and design for your own fallibility.

Because the best time to ask “what could go wrong?” is while you can still change the answer.

sessions.title: An Emergency Decree Walks Into a Pull Request: 165 Years of Italian Law, Read Like a Repo

summary.text: 200,000+ commits. One repository. Every law the Italian state has ever passed, from 1861 to last week. It turns out almost everything Parliament does has a surprisingly clean analogue in a workflow you already use every day — until, suddenly, it doesn't, and the place it stops mapping is exactly the place the constitutional lawyers start arguing. In this talk I'll take you through the corpus as a developer would read it: which legislative moves become one-liners, which ones become traps, and what falls out of git log once you give it 165 years of a country's rulebook to chew on. You'll leave seeing legislation the way you see a codebase — and you'll never read a news headline about a new decree the same way again.

sessions.title: Beyond Benchmarks: What ARC Teaches Us About Measuring Intelligence

summary.text:
Most AI benchmarks measure performance on tasks we can easily collect, score and scale. But do they measure intelligence? Starting from François Chollet’s 2019 paper On the Measure of Intelligence, this talk revisits a century-old question through a modern engineering lens: what should it mean for a machine to learn efficiently, generalize from few examples and solve genuinely novel problems?

We will trace the path from historical ideas of intelligence measurement to ARC, the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus: a benchmark designed around abstract reasoning, minimal priors and tasks that are easy for humans but hard for current AI systems. The goal is not to debate AGI hype, but to understand why benchmark design shapes research, product expectations and our mental models of progress.

Attendees will leave with a clearer framework for reading AI benchmarks critically and asking better questions about “reasoning” claims.

sessions.title: How Far Can You Loop? From one tool call to a Claude Code agent that fixes itself overnight

summary.text:
Every coding agent already runs a loop. Few are designed. The prompt is one turn, the loop is the product: what ships depends on when the agent stops and who agreed it could.
We take Claude Code's loop apart into four parts the model does not own: trigger, exit, verifier and memory. Then we follow them through five rings, from seconds to nights: hooks in the agentic loop, /loop on a clock, /goal with a separate judge, an executed gate with contract and budget, cross-model review on PRs, and a nightly routine that fixes open defects.
Live demos and one real case: an all-green gate, coverage 1.0, that still shipped the wrong code. Because an instruction in a prompt persuades, a hook or an executed check refuses, and no check replaces the person who decides whether it is the right work.
For engineers already using coding agents who want to move from supervised sessions to loops that run with nobody watching.

sessions.title: In attesa dei legali della GRANDE N: come io e Gemini abbiamo portato Parachute su un HW impossibile

summary.text:
Doom gira ovunque, ma Parachute (un Game & Watch Nintendo 1981)?
