sessions.title: One Stack to Observe Them All: Open Source Observability with OpenSearch

summary.text:
What if you could have a complete, production-grade observability platform that is fully open source, built on open standards, and led by The Linux Foundation?

In this session, OpenSearch Ambassador Dotan Horovits demonstrates how OpenSearch delivers a complete, open-source, OpenTelemetry-native observability platform for logs, metrics, traces, APM, and even AI agent observability. You’ll also learn how to integrate with Prometheus metrics, how to create powerful dashboards, and how to easily deploy it to Docker or Kubernetes.

Whether you’re struggling with finding insights in your mounts of logs, fighting a vendors’ bills and proprietary instrumentation, or looking for advanced agentic observability, this session will give you the open source you don’t want to miss.

sessions.title: When NOT to build an agent: Lessons from systems that didn't want autonomy

summary.text:
"Build an agent" has become the default answer to every AI systems question. But autonomy is a feature, not a default. In production systems we've shipped, granting it made things measurably worse: recursive loops burning 20-30x normal token spend, latency drift, boundary violations turning a simple question into an unauthorized action, and evaluation collapsing once a model chose its own path.

Drawing on real systems that failed in traceable ways, we walk through the architectural replacements that fixed them - cutting p99 latency and error rate with the same underlying models.

We'll cover: six failure modes, from recursive loops to the MCP attack surface; what replaced the agent (router patterns, structured output, step-level observability); a two-axis framework for when autonomy earns its place; and a 6-question checklist for your next agentic build.

You'll leave with a mental model for the question that matters more than "can we build an agent": should we?

sessions.title: AI won't fix your Developer Experience

summary.text:
Coding assistant e agenti AI possono rendere gli sviluppatori più veloci, ma non risolvono automaticamente ambienti complessi, pipeline lente, test fragili, documentazione difficile da trovare o processi poco chiari.
Anzi, aumentando la velocità di produzione del codice, l'AI può rendere ancora più evidenti i colli di bottiglia del software delivery lifecycle.
In questo talk vedremo come mappare le developer journey, identificare i reali punti di friction e progettare una Developer Experience capace di evolvere insieme ai nuovi workflow AI-assisted, attraverso esempi e lezioni apprese in Docebo.

sessions.title: Build agents with agents

summary.text:
Coding agents are changing how we write software. But can they change how we build other agents?

In this session, I will show how to use a coding agent, leveraging skills, context management, and structured specs, to design and generate a complex multi-agent architecture with the Google Agent Development Kit (ADK).

The result is a meta-development workflow where the agent drives the architecture, writes the code, and wires up the system, turning hours of scaffolding into a collaborative, spec-to-agent pipeline.

Whether you are new to ADK or already building production agents, this talk will challenge how you think about the role of AI in your development workflow.

sessions.title: Dal codice in banca ai videogiochi: il lungo percorso di un indie

summary.text:
A 40 anni ho lasciato un posto sicuro da responsabile software in banca per fondare uno studio di videogiochi. Non è stato un salto nel vuoto, ma l'arrivo di un lungo percorso.

In questo talk lo racconto: la passione per i videogiochi da bambino, gli anni da informatico tra reti, sviluppo e gestione di team, la parentesi da giornalista, i primi passi sugli app store appena nati, un piccolo lavoro diventato un grande progetto e il lavoro per la Marina americana.

Poi arrivo al cuore del discorso: cosa cambia tra software aziendale e videogiochi, e cosa significa fondare uno studio indipendente. Parlo di difficoltà economiche, di adattamento e di una scoperta scomoda: per fare i giochi che ami, prima devi imparare a vendere.

Un racconto onesto per chi sogna di cambiare strada o di lavorare nei videogiochi.

sessions.title: SCRIBA.AI. soluzione IA italiana per modernizzare il codice legacy

summary.text:
Presentiamo SCRIBA.AI, la soluzione di IA per convertire codice legacy in codice moderno.

Sviluppata interamente in Italia, SCRIBA.AI non è la classica interfaccia per richiamare un modello generalista come ChatGPT o ClaudeCode. Al contrario, ha una struttura di agenti, modelli e orchestratori che convertono - senza tradurre - oltre 100 linguaggi obsoleti in applicativi ISO-equivalenti in linguaggio moderno (Java, Python ecc)

Questo consente di convertire codice in modo completamente automatico, con un risultato di precisione che sfiora il 97%, dunque quasi deterministico.

Durante il Workshop mostreremo il funzionamento della piattaforma, faremo una demo live mostrando il risultato che si riesce ad ottenere, ed offriremo una conversione gratuita ad un partecipante.

SCRIBA.AI ha come missione la modernizzazione dei sistemi informatici del mondo intero; ricerchiamo partner affidabili per questa operazione, questa è la ragione della nostra presenza a Codemotion.

sessions.title: Shutup, Dependency Track! Silencing false positives locally with AST and AI

summary.text:
Modern software is assembled, not just written: nearly 90% of a typical application consists of third-party libraries. If a critical vulnerability like Log4Shell were disclosed tomorrow, how long would it take your team to identify every affected microservice?
In this session, we will explore how to democratize Software Supply Chain Security (SSCS) by building an automated defense perimeter at zero licensing cost. Through a Live Demo featuring a Docker-based prototype, we will walk through a real-world architecture integrating AST analysis, local LLMs, and automated VEX generation.
We will go beyond basic scanning by demonstrating how to leverage Artificial Intelligence for code reachability analysis, generating VEX (Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange) files to silence false positives and focus only on actionable risks. We will also discuss how this stack prepares organizations for the upcoming EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) requirements

sessions.title: The Zero-Temperature Lie: Why Your Deterministic LLM is Still Hallucinating Randomness

summary.text:
Deterministic LLM inference sounds simple: set temperature to zero and get consistent answers. But reality is messier, and asking the same question a thousand times might yield dozens of different responses.

While GPU parallelism and floating-point arithmetic play a role, a study by Thinking Machine Labs identifies the real culprit as… other users. Concurrent requests to the same server change the batch size, which silently alters the order of transformer computations, making the output look like uncontrollable randomness.

This talk will debunk the common myths about LLM nondeterminism, walk through the actual mechanics of inference engines, and explain what it would take to achieve true reproducibility.

Whether calling an external API or running a self-hosted inference stack, attendees will leave with a clear understanding of why this happens, which strategies can help address it, and how to think about reproducibility in AI systems.

sessions.title: What comes after Git?

summary.text: Are the version control system wars over? It mostly looks like that, as Git has been the default contender for more than the past 10 years. But how did that even happen? And what will it take to dethrone the most dominating piece of software our industry has ever seen? New version control systems are rising on the horizon, with promising new features to simplify development workflows and improve developer experience, that are often inherently complex, or even outright impossible, to do with Git. In this talk, we are going to take a look at the history of version control systems, how new rising young stars like Jujutsu, Sapling or GitButler are innovating in that space today and how to use and integrate them into your existing Git-based project.

sessions.title: Why Coding Agents Need You More Than Ever

summary.text:
“Will AI make developers obsolete?” The hype says the developer is finished. The denial says it’s just autocomplete. Both are comforting false simplicity.

Capable coding agents don’t make software engineering obsolete; they make it indispensable. An LLM is a remarkable generative engine, but by its architecture, it has no internal reference for correctness, no grasp of the domain it is building for, no orientation toward the system’s future, and no memory across sessions. That isn’t a benchmark gap the next model closes; it’s a structural vacuum.

Filling it takes method, domain knowledge, design judgment, process, and engineering depth to distinguish the correct from the merely plausible. The quality problems of AI-generated software are exactly why coding and design skills matter more, not less.

The uncomfortable, liberating consequence: capable agents demand more software engineering, not less. The discipline isn’t in decline. Its moment has arrived.

sessions.title: AI Fundamentals in Action: Evolving a Flappy Bird Agent

summary.text:
We use LLMs every day, but how many of us could explain what's actually happening under the hood? This talk explores the fundamentals behind modern AI through a small, fully transparent agent that learns to play Flappy Bird.

Starting from the familiar Transformer architecture, we zoom in step by step to explore the feed-forward neural network. We then look at how these concepts translate into working code, using a Flappy Bird implementation built with Compose Multiplatform as our playground.

First, we let a neural network with random, untrained weights take control. Unsurprisingly, it plays terribly. With no labeled dataset to train on, we introduce a genetic algorithm: a population of networks, a simple fitness signal, and successive generations of selection, crossover, and mutation. As the algorithm runs, we watch random behavior evolve into a competent player.

Through code walkthroughs and visual demonstrations, we unpack each component of the process, making neural networks and evolutionary algorithms tangible without getting lost in mathematical formalism.

No black boxes, no magic: just a neural network, an evolutionary process, and a clear look at how they work together. Attendees will leave with an intuitive understanding of these AI fundamentals and why they still matter in the age of LLMs.

sessions.title: Game Audio: Beyond PlaySound()

summary.text: Dalla semplice riproduzione di suoni ai moderni sistemi audio interattivi. Attraverso esempi pratici di integrazione audio in Unreal Engine, vedremo come eventi e parametri di gioco permettano agli audio designer di costruire sistemi sonori complessi, in collaborazione con i programmatori.

sessions.title: How to Interview Engineers in the AI Era: What I Changed and What Actually Works

summary.text:
AI has fundamentally changed how engineers work, but most hiring processes haven't changed at all.

Coding assistants can generate solutions in seconds. System design answers can be refined with prompts. Candidates walk into interviews with powerful AI tools at their side. Yet many companies are still evaluating engineers as if AI didn't exist.

After interviewing hundreds of engineers at Elementor, I redesigned my hiring process for the AI era. I changed what we evaluate. Today we test how engineers think, how they collaborate with AI, and how they apply judgment when AI-generated solutions are incomplete, incorrect, or misleading.

In this talk, I'll share what changed in our hiring process and what actually works in practice.

Whether you're hiring engineers, preparing for interviews, or leading an engineering organization, you'll leave with a practical framework for evaluating engineering talent in the AI era.

sessions.title: How to tame our Hermes minions fleet

summary.text:
Spin up a VPS, run `install.sh`, plug in a Telegram bot token, and boom - our first Hermes AI agent is alive. A couple of prompts and it is already sending news reports, organizing emails, and build our second brain. It feels effortless, almost magical. We add more minions and turn everything into a workflow. Until a month later, we realize we're spending more time firefighting and patching issues than building anything new.

This talk distills months of lost sleep trying to tame the bill that non-deterministic agentic workflows inevitably hands us. We'll dive into skill design, organizational patterns, and harness support tools. Using a Hermes Agent and personal productivity as example, but with principles applicable across the board.

sessions.title: Saliresti su un aereo vibecodato? Spec-driven AI con EARS e Walden

summary.text:
Partendo da un sistema critico come quello che governa i motori di un aereo, esploreremo perché la vera sfida del vibe coding non è generare più codice, ma definire specifiche chiare, governare ciò che chiediamo all’AI di costruire e verificarne il risultato.
Introdurremo EARS (Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax), una sintassi leggera per esprimere requisiti chiari e verificabili, e useremo Walden, un kernel CLI open source, per collegare requisiti, design, task e verifiche eseguibili.
Vedremo infine come queste metodologie siano portate su scala con il framework di Agentic Software Delivery di Engineering che integra tracciabilità, verificabilità e controllo lungo l’intero Software Development Lifecycle.

sessions.title: The Swiss cheese fix: why PR quality needs layers

summary.text:
PRs sitting unreviewed for days. Reviewers skimming 500-line diffs. Rubber-stamp approvals on changes nobody fully understood. Most engineering teams quietly accepted that PR reviews were a known weak point as the cost of moving fast.

Then AI coding agents arrived and made it unsustainable, flooding review queues with high-volume, low-quality PRs.

The fix isn't a single solution. It's layers.

This talk introduces the Swiss cheese model as a framework for thinking about PR quality: stack enough imperfect defensive layers and you get a system more reliable than any individual component. The emerging layers (spec-driven development, multi-agent competition, automated verification, and giving agents the right runtime context from the start, etc.) each address a specific failure mode. None of them are mutually exclusive.

What you'll leave with: a concrete mental model for where your current review process is failing and what a layered verification system looks like.

sessions.title: Configurare l’harness: da Claude Code come tool a Claude Code come sistema di lavoro

summary.text:
Un coding agent moderno arriva già con il suo harness. Quello che cambia i risultati non è costruirne uno, è configurarlo. In questa sessione si lavora su Claude Code come implementazione di riferimento e si attraversano le superfici che governano davvero il comportamento dell’agente: istruzioni di progetto, skill, permessi, hook, subagent, MCP, fino al plugin che impacchetta la configurazione e la rende condivisibile nel team.
Il filo conduttore non è il tutorial, è la decisione: quale superficie deve possedere quale regola. Una conoscenza contestuale non è un hook, un vincolo che deve valere sempre non è una riga di istruzioni. Poi si apre il loop a grafo, con subagent in parallelo e un nodo di giudizio, e si verifica se serva davvero. Le decisioni si trasferiscono agli altri coding agent: cambiano i nomi dei file, non il ragionamento.

sessions.title: Honey, We Predicted the Bits

summary.text:
80s sci-fi movies gave us rays that miniaturized humans and things without losing a single atom. That's what we call "lossless" compression in computing, where we want to shrink web assets, code, and payloads where 100% bit fidelity is non-negotiable.

As an article that circulated a lot this summer states, compression is prediction. The better a system can predict what comes next, the fewer bits we need to transmit. But we have real engineering constraints!

In this talk, we will explore:

- The classical and modern web stack, how we evolved from basic redundancy to today's landscape
- Why the model must be part of the message
- The format-aware frontier, so how OpenZL uses DAGs, structural knowledge and universal decompressors
- The connection with LLMs, where the prediction of the next token and the cross-entropy loss are mathematically identical to optimal entropy coding... and why language models are great predictors, but impractical compressors

sessions.title: Text-to-SQL Isn't Enough: Trustworthy AI Data Agents on a Semantic Layer

summary.text:
Ask an LLM "how many policies did each agency sell last quarter?" and let it write SQL. It works in the demo, much less in production: it invents JOINs, forgets filters, picks the wrong granularity, and business logic leaks from data models into prompts.
A semantic layer fixes this: metrics are defined once, versioned with your data models and compiled into correct SQL. The model selects, the semantic layer computes. Mistakes become visible instead of plausible.
We share how we built Flowmetrics, an internal tool on top of open-source MetricFlow. It gives AI agents governed access to metrics via a Python library, an MCP server and versioned agent skills. Through code, we cover hybrid search for metric discovery, saved queries as canonical answers, row-level security the LLM can't bypass, and design decisions we had to revisit.
You'll leave with patterns for any semantic layer and a live demo on a real insurance use case.

sessions.title: The case for Small Models: a 1M ModernBERT playing Doom in milliseconds

summary.text:
Frontier LLMs get the headlines, but a lot of production AI runs on small, specialized models, where cost and latency matter more than raw capability.
In this talk, I’ll push that idea to its limit by training a tiny 1M-parameter ModernBERT model to play Doom on a CPU.

We’ll explore why encoder architectures are making a comeback through projects like ModernBERT and GLiNER, and look at practical use cases like embedding retrieval, information extraction, anonymization, and safety guardrails.

Then I’ll walk through the Doom player training: the architecture, Supervised Fine-Tuning from human gameplay, and Reinforcement Learning for autonomous improvement, all trained and deployed on consumer hardware. Getting there meant several failed attempts, and I’ll share lessons from them.

By the end, you'll know when small encoder models are the right tool, and you’ll see one playing Doom in real time.

sessions.title: The Ultimate Kubernetes Challenge: An Interactive Trivia Game on concepts, components, usage...

summary.text:
Kubernetes has become the de facto standard for deploying and operating containerized applications. We use it, as well as its ecosystem, on a daily basis, but do we know them as well as we think we do?

With a mix of quiz and live demos, come learn and/or improve your knowledge. You will discover (or rediscover) the key concepts of Kubernetes (pods, secrets, services...), internal components but also best practices.

In this fun and dynamic talk, come compete throughout the quiz and explore the wonderful world of Kubernetes.

Icing on the cake: the first will win some swags.

sessions.title: Trovare la Propria Dimensione

summary.text:
Drawing on the experience Antab Studio has gained over its ten years of activity, we will highlight the deep synergy that exists between business management, technical and creative decision-making, software design, and day-to-day development. In this sense, the talk takes the form of a somewhat unconventional post-mortem, examining the two titles we have released as an independent micro-team.
After sharing our experience, we would like to leave time for questions and discussion with the audience.

sessions.title: Accessibility first: progettare una piattaforma quando l’accessibilità non è negoziabile

summary.text:
Cosa succede quando l’accessibilità non è una feature da aggiungere, ma il requisito fondamentale su cui costruire tutto?

In questo talk racconteremo lo sviluppo del nuovo ecosistema di gestione eventi di Accessibility Days, progettato con un approccio realmente accessibility first.

La differenza, questa volta, era concreta: molte delle persone che utilizzano quotidianamente questi strumenti sono persone con disabilità.

Partendo da esigenze reali, mostreremo come l’accessibilità abbia influenzato architettura, frontend, componenti e workflow fin dalle prime decisioni progettuali.

sessions.title: Provocazioni Artificiali: un talk così “shiftato” che ti verrà la voglia di rubarci il microfono!

summary.text:
Il SaaS è morto? Le aziende di consulenza falliranno in 18 mesi? Cosa succede se un Senior Dev scopre di essere solo un Junior che conosce a memoria le API? È possibile una startup da un miliardo con un solo dipendente?
In questo talk interattivo, Daniel e Stefano lanceranno sul palco le provocazioni più scottanti su business, competenze e mercato del lavoro stravolti dall’AI. Regola numero uno: siamo tutti speaker e se parli non verrai giudicato da nessuno. Se una tesi ti sembra una follia, prendi il microfono e ribaltala.
Esagerando le previsioni cercheremo il confine tra distopia e opportunità, per portarci a casa qualcosa di più del semplice hype: una visione aperta, critica e maledettamente creativa.
Il nostro obiettivo è quello di dare ai partecipanti argomenti da approfondire durante le prossime pause caffè e qualche spunto per reinventare il nostro lavoro.
Porta la tua idea, la tua esperienza e un bel po’ di spirito critico. Ne avremo bisogno.

sessions.title: Scaling AI Adoption: The Real Challenges of Transforming 300 Engineers

summary.text:
Most companies talk about becoming “AI-native.” Very few actually do it.

In this talk, I’ll share how we’re approaching the upskilling of ~300 engineers to move beyond experimentation and into real, repeatable AI-native development.

We’ll cover how we’re introducing new paradigms like AI-Native Engineering (AINE) and Spec-Driven Development, how we’re structuring the individual contributor journey, and how we’re driving adoption across teams with very different levels of maturity.

More importantly, we’ll dive into what doesn’t work: resistance patterns, false starts, over-reliance on tools, and the gap between perceived and actual productivity gains.

This talk will give you a concrete blueprint along with the trade-offs and lessons learned along the way.

sessions.title: Critica dell'informatica pura

summary.text:
Le schede perforate, le macchine calcolatrici programmabili, gli operatori booleani, gli automi, le architetture di calcolo parallelo, le funzioni ricorsive, le lambda: sono solo esempi di concetti che gli informatici credono di aver scoperto, ma che in realtà hanno solo riscoperto dopo che alcuni filosofi, magari secoli prima, le avevano pensate.

Cosa possiamo imparare da questa storia? Che possiamo credere d’essere il miglior programmatore, architetto, informatico del mondo, ma molto probabilmente non lo siamo, e il miglior modo per diventarlo è capire di non esserlo.

Il talk sarà disseminato di esempi tecnici, per cuori impavidi e menti aperte, somministrati in modo giocoso ma rigoroso perché, "quanno se gioca bisogna esse' seri".

sessions.title: Inclusion by design: engineering team workflows for different brains

summary.text:
Engineering teams obsess over system design, yet many still run on workflows that only work for one kind of brain. The result is familiar friction: ambiguous meetings, noisy emails, unclear requirements, and fragile onboarding. This talk treats inclusion not as a slogan but as an engineering problem: if a workflow only works for a narrow cognitive profile, it is badly designed.
I will share practical patterns to redesign technical collaboration (yes, I will show code!), models for decision‑making, checklists, case studies from large‑scale, legacy environments. I draw on three sources: my activism and lived experience as a neurodivergent professional, my legal training and nearly two decades at the intersection of law and technology, and a career inside major Italian tech and finance organisations where I’ve seen what breaks and what works. This session is for tech leads and IT managers who want to reduce ambiguity and build workflows that scale across different cognitive profiles.
